source_name: IMF Article IV consultation staff reports - Republic of North Macedonia
why_relevant: Annual independent assessment of the MK banking and financial system with data annexes (credit growth, bank concentration, deposits, payment/financial-sector reform commitments including SEPA); also documents Selected Issues papers on digitalisation.

source_name: IMF eLibrary - North Macedonia country report series
why_relevant: Structured XML/HTML rendering of the same country reports, easier to parse than PDFs and gives a full archive back-catalogue for time-series extraction.

source_name: European Commission Enlargement Package - North Macedonia country report
why_relevant: Annual accession progress report includes chapters on free movement of capital, financial services and payment systems; documents alignment with PSD2/SEPA, supervisory capacity and outstanding legislative gaps that shape the MK payments market.

source_name: Ministry of European Affairs (MEP) - EC reports and Growth Plan / Reform Agenda pages (Macedonian)
why_relevant: Macedonian-language mirror and index of EC country reports, the Reform Agenda 2024-2027 and Growth Plan milestones (incl. SEPA accession), plus payment-request/monitoring news - the local gateway into the EU donor layer.

source_name: EU Reform and Growth Facility - Reform Agenda for North Macedonia 2024-2027
why_relevant: The Reform Agenda binds disbursements to specific payment-market steps (SEPA membership, payment-services law alignment, digitalisation of public payments); its indicator tables are a forward calendar of MK payment-market change.

source_name: European Commission - North Macedonia financial assistance under IPA
why_relevant: Authoritative index of IPA II/III programming documents and action fiches for MK; action fiches describe baseline market conditions (e.g. digital public services, PFM, e-payments) and the budget behind them.

source_name: EU Funding & Tenders Portal (EuropeAid prospect and call details, .../ACT/MK references)
why_relevant: Forward-looking pipeline of EU-funded actions for MK before they reach TED; prospect notices give sector, indicative budget and timing for digitalisation/financial-sector actions.

source_name: EBRD Project Summary Documents (PSD) search - North Macedonia financial institutions
why_relevant: PSDs disclose counterparty bank, amount, purpose and expected transition impact for EBRD credit lines to MK banks (Go Digital Western Balkans, SME digitalisation with Sparkasse and NLB Banka Skopje) - a running record of who is funding MK bank digitalisation and how much.

source_name: EBRD North Macedonia country strategy and results snapshot
why_relevant: Country strategy and diagnostics set out EBRD's read of MK financial-sector gaps (digitalisation, access to finance, capital markets) and the planned pipeline - useful as an independent structural assessment of the market.

source_name: World Bank projects & operations - North Macedonia (incl. NODE P170993)
why_relevant: Project appraisal documents, results frameworks and implementation status reports for MK digital-economy and financial-sector operations contain baseline/target indicators on digital payments, connectivity and government e-payments.

source_name: World Bank Documents & Reports - North Macedonia policy notes and country economic reports
why_relevant: Policy notes and Western Balkans Regular Economic Reports contain analysis on MK payment-system modernisation, SEPA entry and cross-border payment costs, often with original charts not published locally.

source_name: World Bank Global Payment Systems Survey (GPSS)
why_relevant: Periodic central-bank-reported survey of payment system infrastructure (RTGS, ACH, card switches, retail instruments, oversight) with country-level responses; the main supranational description of MK payment infrastructure design.

source_name: World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide (RPW)
why_relevant: Quarterly corridor-level pricing of cross-border transfers; MK is a significant remittance-receiving economy, so corridor pricing and instrument mix (cash pickup vs account vs card) proxies cash-versus-digital behaviour.

source_name: Council of Europe Development Bank (CEB) - North Macedonia country page and project disclosures
why_relevant: CEB lends to the Development Bank of North Macedonia and microfinance institutions (e.g. Horizonti), so its disclosures map on-lending channels and financial-inclusion funding, though it does not fund payment infrastructure directly.

source_name: EEAS / EU Delegation to North Macedonia
why_relevant: Announces IPA calls, Growth Plan disbursements, subcommittee meetings on economic and financial issues and statistics; a reliable early signal of donor-funded activity touching MK payments before formal documents publish.

source_name: OpenTender / Open Contracting Data Registry - TED-derived European procurement data
why_relevant: Structured, cleaned OCDS re-publication of TED notices; far easier to query at scale for MK-related EU-funded contracts than TED's own interface, and it also aggregates national procurement data.

source_name: Ministry of Finance of North Macedonia - ESPEO / EU economic reporting pages (Macedonian)
why_relevant: Hosts the Macedonian-language reporting that feeds the EU economic dialogue (Economic Reform Programme and related reports), the national counterpart to EC/IMF assessments and often the first place their underlying tables appear locally.

source_name: Комерцијална банка АД Скопје — investor/annual reports & presentations (kb.mk)
why_relevant: Largest domestic bank by card issuing and second-largest ATM network; its annual reports (годишен извештај) and periodic investor presentations quantify branch/ATM/POS network, card portfolio and payment-operations fee income. A June 2025 investor presentation PDF was surfaced directly (KB-PREZENTACIJA-30062025.pdf), showing presentations are published on a recurring quarterly/semi-annual cadence.

source_name: Стопанска банка АД — Скопје (NBG/OTP group) financial & annual reports (stb.com.mk)
source_subtype: bank annual report / audited financial statements
why_relevant: Publishes a full 'Годишен извештај за работењето' each April containing explicit YoY growth rates for digital-banking active users, card transaction volumes, POS/e-commerce payment growth and number of card-accepting merchant points — exactly the A4 card/POS metrics, expressed as percentages rather than absolute counts.

source_name: НЛБ Банка АД Скопје — годишни финансиски извештаи (nlb.mk)
why_relevant: Third-largest MK bank and an NLB Group subsidiary; dedicated annual-financial-reports landing page. Also publishes the regulatory 'персонализиран годишен извештај за надоместоци за платежните услуги' notice, which points to the payment-services fee framework (PSD2-style fee statements) relevant to payment-fee benchmarking.

source_name: NLB Group investor relations — group reports with North Macedonia segment (nlb.si / nlbgroup.com)
why_relevant: Parent-group quarterly reports and results presentations break out the North Macedonia market (loans, deposits, digital penetration, client counts) with more standardised and more frequent disclosure than the local subsidiary — classic 'parent says more than the local entity' case. NLB also owns Komercijalna banka Skopje's Serbian namesake and holds ~87% of NLB Banka Skopje.

source_name: Халкбанк АД Скопје — Извештаи (годишни извештаи) page
source_subtype: bank annual report page + ATM locator
why_relevant: Halkbank MK publishes individual and consolidated audited annual reports; separately it operates a distribution partnership making its services available through 327 active post-office units, which is a rare quantified data point on physical payment-access points outside the ATM/POS fleet. It also maintains an ATM map page (atm-mapa.nspx) that can be mined for ATM counts and geography.

source_name: Шпаркасе Банка Македонија АД Скопје — Финансиски извештаи (sparkasse.mk)
why_relevant: Dedicated reports section carrying annual reports and audited statements across multiple years, with historical English-language annual reports also on the same CMS path — bilingual coverage makes it one of the easier MK banks to parse. Subsidiary of Steiermärkische Bank und Sparkassen AG (Erste/Sparkassen orbit), so parent disclosures are a second route.

source_name: ПроКредит Банка АД Скопје — annual reports (pcb.mk)
why_relevant: Publishes English-language annual reports including a merged IFRS 2024 document; ProCredit MK is a 'direct banking' model (branch-light, self-service zones and 24/7 ATM zones), so its reports are unusually informative on cash-handling migration, deposit ATMs and digital channel adoption — a strong indirect read on cash usage trends.

source_name: ProCredit Holding AG — group annual reports, Pillar 3 and country-by-country reporting
why_relevant: Group reports carry a per-country segment (North Macedonia) with headcount, branch counts, turnover and tax by jurisdiction (CbCR), plus the group Pillar-3 disclosure required under EU CRR 575/2013 — a standardised, comparable annual series that the local entity does not replicate. Confirmed live cadence: a 2025 Annual Report PDF is already published (March 2026).

source_name: УНИБанка АД Скопје — годишен извештај / shareholder assembly materials (unibank.mk)
why_relevant: Mid-sized bank publishing its full annual report as a numbered item in the ordinary general-assembly document pack, alongside a corporate-governance code — the assembly pack is a reliable, dated annual container for operating and payments narrative.

source_name: Силк Роуд Банка АД Скопје — financial statements filed via MSE announcements
why_relevant: Small bank whose audited statements (MK and English versions) surface primarily as MSE announcement PDFs rather than on a well-structured own-site reports page; the MSE Announcement166 repository is the practical retrieval route for this issuer.

source_name: Развојна банка на Северна Македонија АД Скопје (MBDP) — corporate site
why_relevant: The country's only development bank, 100% state-owned, established by special law (Закон за Развојната банка). Not a card/ATM issuer, so of low value for payments-fleet metrics, but useful as a boundary case and for state-guarantee/export-credit context; its governing law is mirrored on the NBRM site.
